title: The blessing to carry (Numbers 6:24–26)
hook: the Lord bless you and keep you, and give you peace
carry: the lord bless you and keep you
tomorrow: can you be excited and terrified about the same thing?

segments.voice: Yesterday, your rule of life: a path to walk by or a yoke to avoid, both in Paul, and a few plain lines for tomorrow. The rule goes on.

Someone says your name across a loud room, and your head turns before you've decided to turn it. A name said warmly lands in the body. One blessing in the book of Numbers is built that way. "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee." Listen to the small word. Thee. In the King James, thee is one person. Not you all. You. The priests stood before a whole people, and the words were shaped for each one of them.
screen: `YOUR NAME ACROSS A ROOM.` → `THEE: ONE PERSON.` → `SHAPED FOR EACH ONE.`

segments.voice: In Numbers, God tells Moses to tell Aaron and his sons, "On this wise ye shall bless the children of Israel." Then the words: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace." Feel what each line does. Keep: guarded, watched over, the way shepherds keep a flock by night. A face that shines: someone turning toward you with light in their face, glad you're there. A countenance lifted up: being looked at, not past. And peace, the last gift, the one the whole blessing walks toward. These were Israel's words first, and Jews pray them still; some churches speak them over people at the end of a service. Then the next verse: "they shall put my name upon the children of Israel; and I will bless them." The priest speaks; God blesses. The one saying it passes it on, and never owns it. That's why the blessing can travel. A parent can say it over a sleeping child. A friend can say it beside a hospital bed. And a person can say it over themselves on the way out the door.
screen: `KEEP: WATCHED OVER.` · `A FACE THAT SHINES.` · `LOOKED AT, NOT PAST.` · `THE PRIEST SPEAKS; GOD BLESSES.` · then, large: `THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU.`

segments.voice: Say the blessing out loud over yourself, slowly, one line to a breath, and hear your own voice say thee. Then say it again with one person's name in it, as if they were sitting across from you.
The blessing to carry. Three lines from Numbers, worded for one person at a time: bless and keep, shine and be gracious, lift up and give peace.
Your line: the lord bless you and keep you. The priests spoke it, and passed it on. Peace to you.

howItsDone: Jews pray the priestly blessing in the synagogue, and some churches close their services with it, the minister raising a hand or both hands over the people.

fork.setup: a teacher closes graduation by saying Numbers 6 over the whole class. why is it worded "thee," not "you all"?
options: an old printing slip in the King James.
it was first written for a single king.
it's shaped for each person, one at a time.
fork.reveal: spoken over a whole people, the blessing addresses each one: thee, singular. in a crowd, every person hears their own blessing.

original.note: Hebrew: may he bless you (one person). the first word of the blessing in Numbers 6:24.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice closing line at the end of a church service.
what it means: a blessing worded for one person at a time, passed on and never owned.
what a scholar hears: the Hebrew forms in Numbers 6:24–26 are singular, and 6:27 makes God, not the priest, the one who blesses.

a prayer said before meals in Israel's homes
a farewell speech Moses gave before he died

chat.says: pop wants to bless me at sunday dinner before orientation. what do i even do with my hands lol
options: Just receive it. Pop speaks the words, but in Numbers it is God who blesses.
Bless him back right away, line for line, so it isn't one-sided.
Bow low and pray hard the whole time, or the blessing might not take.
chat.meaning: In Numbers 6:27 the priests put God's name on the people, 'and I will bless them.' The one speaking passes it on; you only receive.

Numbers.meaning: the fourth book of the Bible, Israel's years in the wilderness
